title: Two moving clocks and one simultaneity slice
promptMarkdown: Two clocks at rest in $S\prime$ are synchronised there and separated by $L\prime=120\,\mathrm m$ along their direction of motion. The frame moves at $v=3c/5$ relative to $S$. Derive the simultaneous-in-$S$ separation and the difference of their displayed times, leading minus trailing. Then determine how much each display advances during $1\,\mu\mathrm s$ of $S$ time. Explain why an offset does not imply different clock rates.
hintLadder: Apply both Lorentz equations to the same two simultaneous-in-$S$ events.
For a clock rate use $dx=vdt$, not $dx=0$.
Draw both parallel clock worldlines and a horizontal $S$ slice.
